# Create combat gym scene for combat-coupled power-ups (P3 Shield, P4 Bomb, P6 Phase Shift, P7 Teleport) with low-level enemy threats

## Problem statement

Four power-up types in the GDD catalogue — **P3 Shield, P4 Bomb, P6 Phase Shift, P7 Teleport** — cannot demonstrate their full behaviour without threats: Shield must absorb a hit, Bomb must clear on-screen enemy bullets, Phase Shift must pass through enemies and bullets, and Teleport must search for a safe spot free of threats. The operator split these "combat-coupled" types out of the threat-free power-up gym (AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT) into this dedicated **combat gym scene** that contains a **low-level enemy threat (E1 Scout with shooting)**. The scene shares the round-robin spawn lifecycle, grow-shrink animation, 3% collection threshold, player ship, and standalone HUD class with the non-combat gym, on which this item depends.

## Users

- **Player / developer testing the game** — wants to see each combat-coupled power-up's full effect against real (but low-level) threats: a shield bubble popping on a hit, a bomb wiping a bullet cloud, ghosting straight through a formation, and blinking away to a safe spot.
- **AI agents / developers implementing AI_Hell** — need the threat-coupled behaviour (hit absorption, bullet clearing, intangibility, safe-spot resolution) implemented and tested once, in a form the main game can reuse.

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, I want my shield bubble to absorb exactly one hit and pop, so I can verify the GDD's "absorbs one hit" rule.
- As a **player**, I want to collect a Bomb while scouts are firing and see every on-screen enemy bullet vanish, with enemies untouched (they are 1 HP, GDD §4.4).
- As a **player**, I want Phase Shift to let me fly straight through the scout formation and its bullets without being hit, for 3 seconds.
- As a **player**, I want to press Space with a collected Teleport to jump to the nearest safe spot (free of scouts and bullets) along my travel direction, gaining Phase Shift on arrival.
- As a **developer**, I want the ship's hit response (no shield/phase shift) to be a simple flash/reset with no lives counter, so the demo keeps a pure combat focus.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Combat scene with ship + low-level threats:** A new `GymPowerUpsCombat` scene (key `GymPowerUpsCombat`, label `PowerUps Combat`) is defined in `src/scenes/gym/`, auto-discovered and listed by the gym index, boots correctly, renders the player ship with standard thrust movement + screen-wrap, and contains a **formation of E1 Scout enemies** (reusing `src/entities/Scout.ts` + the formation utilities) with a **SHOOT toggle** that enables aimed enemy fire at the **ship's live position** (not the fixed demo target), so hits are demonstrable. Shared "← INDEX" back button present.
- [ ] **AC2 — Round-robin spawn/lifecycle:** The scene spawns exactly the combat-coupled power-ups **P3, P4, P6, P7 in ascending GDD order**, one every 5 s, each remaining stationary for a 5 s lifetime; spawn = **grow from scale 0 to full size**, despawn = **shrink to nothing**; growth/shrink delta-time driven with the same tunable constants as the non-combat gym (AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT).
- [ ] **AC3 — Collection rule:** A drop is collectible only while its current scale is **> 3% of full size** (grow, hold, and shrink until below threshold); collection requires the ship to overlap the drop; an uncollected drop fades with no effect.
- [ ] **AC4 — P3 Shield full behaviour:** Collecting P3 arms a shield bubble rendered around the ship for **15 s**; the bubble **absorbs exactly one hit** (enemy body or enemy bullet) and then pops (effect ends, no ship flash/reset for that hit); if never hit, it expires after 15 s. Re-collection while active refreshes the timer to 15 s.
- [ ] **AC5 — P4 Bomb full behaviour:** Collecting P4 instantly removes **all on-screen enemy bullets** (aimed scout fire in-flight), does **not damage enemies** (GDD §4.4 note), is not a timed effect, and shows a brief HUD notice. Re-collection while enemies are not firing is a benign no-op (bullets cleared anyway).
- [ ] **AC6 — P6 Phase Shift full behaviour:** Collecting P6 renders a ghost-outline ship for **3 s** during which the ship **passes through enemy bodies and enemy bullets without being hit**; hit checks are disabled for the duration. Re-collection refreshes the timer to 3 s.
- [ ] **AC7 — P7 Teleport full behaviour:** P7 **stacks FIFO** (each pickup = one use); pressing **Space** consumes the earliest-collected use and teleports the ship **along the current travel direction to the nearest safe spot** — a position free of enemy bodies and enemy bullets in a safety radius, clamped to screen bounds; if no safe spot exists in the travel direction, the ship teleports to the nearest on-screen safe position anyway; on arrival the ship **gains P6 Phase Shift (3 s)** per GDD. HUD shows the teleport count.
- [ ] **AC8 — Hit response (no shield/phase shift):** Being hit by an enemy body or enemy bullet with no active P3/P6 triggers a **simple flash/reset with no lives counter** (e.g., brief invulnerability + reposition), per operator decision; this is the only consequence — no lives, no game over.
- [ ] **AC9 — HUD reuse:** The scene uses the **standalone HUD class from AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT** (`src/ui/HUD.ts`) unchanged for active-effect icons, names, timers (P3/P6), and counts (P7); **no lives counter** in this scene; the HUD class itself is not modified with gym/combat-specific logic (any extension lives in the scene).
- [ ] **AC10 — Testing/validation:** Unit tests cover: P3 absorb-then-pop on a hit + 15 s expiry + refresh; P4 clearing all bullets without enemy damage; P6 pass-through (no hits during 3 s) + refresh; P7 FIFO stack/consume, safe-spot resolution (avoiding scouts/bullets, clamped), fallback when no safe spot, and P6-on-arrival; hit-response flash/reset (no lives); round-robin order. Scene-level tests (gameHarness) verify discovery, ship presence, scout formation + SHOOT toggle, collection against live bullets, and back button. Full suite green.
- [ ] **AC11 — Documentation:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (GDD §6.4 architecture gains `GymPowerUpsCombat`).
- [ ] **AC12 — Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Engine/stack:** Phaser v4 + TypeScript, Vite, Vitest (locked). Neon-vector aesthetic; code-drawn graphics only — **no external art assets**; icons code-drawn per GDD §4.4 suggestions.
- **Threats:** **E1 Scout only** (operator decision) — reuse `src/entities/Scout.ts` as-is; formation via existing utilities; **shooting toggle** enabled for the demo (bullets aimed at the ship's live position). No E2/E3/E4/E5/Boss.
- **No lives model:** hit response is flash/reset only (operator decision); P8 lives is out of scope (it lives in the non-combat gym).
- **Weapon power-ups out of scope:** P1/P2/new weapon patterns belong to AH-0MTC1TEXR006I5XR; the ship's auto-fire is NOT part of this scene (Bomb does not damage enemies, so no fire needed).
- **Shared mechanics:** the spawn cadence (one per 5 s, 5 s lifetime, 0.5 s grow/shrink) and the 3% collection threshold match the non-combat gym (AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT); constants stay in `src/core/constants.ts`; the HUD class is reused unchanged (dependency on that item).
- **Hit model details:** overlap = ship hull radius + enemy/bullet radius, exactly as the GDD "enemies are the bullets" §2.4 model; shield/phase-shift suppress the hit response; teleport safe radius is a tunable constant (proposal: ~3× ship size).

## Existing state

- Non-combat power-up gym **AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT** (intake_complete, open) delivers, first: `src/powerups/PowerUp.ts` (base lifecycle), the type catalogue + icons, `src/ui/HUD.ts` (standalone), the spawn/lifecycle constants, and `GymPowerUps` — **this item depends on those reusable pieces**. This item adds the P3/P4/P6/P7 catalogue entries + threat-coupled effect hooks.
- `src/entities/Scout.ts` exists with `tryFireAimedBullet` (currently aimed at a fixed demo target), formation offsets, alive/destroy lifecycle; `GymScout` demonstrates a V-formation with EXPLODE/SHOOT buttons via the shared `GymFormationScene` core library (`src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`).
- Ship + thrust movement exist (`src/entities/Player.ts`, `src/utils/movement.ts`, `GymPlayer.ts`).
- GDD §4.4 defines P3/P4/P6/P7 semantics and icon suggestions; §4.4 notes Bomb does not damage 1-HP enemies; §2.3 lives model (out of scope here, replaced by flash/reset).
- Tests use Vitest + a gameHarness (`src/test/gameHarness.ts`) with happy-dom.

## Desired change

1. Extend the power-up catalogue from AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT with **P3/P4/P6/P7** entries (id, name, icon, duration/stack semantics, threat-coupled effect hooks), following the same `src/powerups/` layout.
2. Add `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` — ship (reused `Player` + movement), a Scout V-formation with a SHOOT toggle (bullets aimed at the ship), the shared round-robin spawner (P3 → P4 → P6 → P7), grow/hold/shrink lifecycle, 3% collection gate, threat-coupled effect application (shield absorb, bomb clear, phase shift pass-through, teleport safe-spot), flash/reset hit response, HUD attachment (reused), back button.
3. Ship-aimed fire: extend or parameterise the Scout's fire target so bullets aim at the ship's live position (implementation may pass the ship position into the scene's fire-collection path).
4. Add safe-spot resolution (enemy/bullet-aware) + teleport consumption to `src/powerups/effects.ts`; add hit-check suppression for shield/phase-shift in the scene collision pass.
5. Update the GDD §6.4 architecture briefly (list `GymPowerUpsCombat`; note threat-coupled effects as implemented).
6. Tests: unit tests for P3/P4/P6/P7 behaviours + scene tests via gameHarness.

## Key Files:

- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` — **new** combat gym scene (the deliverable).
- `src/powerups/types.ts` — extend the catalogue from AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT with **P3/P4/P6/P7** entries.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — extend with shield-absorb state, bomb bullet-clear, phase-shift hit suppression, teleport safe-spot resolution + FIFO consumption.
- `src/powerups/icons.ts` — extend with P3/P4/P6/P7 code-drawn icons.
- `src/powerups/PowerUp.ts` — **reused** (depends on AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT).
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — **reused unchanged** (depends on AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT).
- `src/entities/Scout.ts` — possibly parameterised aim target (ship position) for `tryFireAimedBullet`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.test.ts` (+ P3/P4/P6/P7 unit tests) — **new** tests.
- `src/core/constants.ts` — teleport safe radius + travelled distance, hit-reset values (extend the shared constants).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §6.4 architecture: add `GymPowerUpsCombat`.

## Related work

- **AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT** — "Create gym scene for power-ups with spawning, collection, and standalone HUD" (the non-combat gym): **prerequisite** — supplies the shared PowerUp lifecycle, catalogue, icons, HUD class, and spawn/lifecycle constants this item reuses/extends. Dependency edge: this item → AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT.
- **AH-0MTC1TEXR006I5XR** — "Weapon power-ups (3 patterns + reset) with auto-fire and weapon gym scene" (in-progress): sibling — weapon power-ups excluded here, same round-robin/grow-shrink/3% mechanics.
- **"Create E1 Scout gym scene" / GymScout** — precedent for the Scout formation, EXPLODE/SHOOT buttons, and the `GymFormationScene` core-library pattern (AH-0MT994ESD000RP1Q completed; core-library refactor AH-0MT987VA3005YBNK / AH-0MTAN4IFR007U9B3 completed).
- **"Create gym scene with player ship and thrust-based space movement" (AH-0MT97OA3E001DOYW)** — precedent for `Player` reuse.
- GDD power-up catalog items (completed): "Redesign P7 Dash…" (AH-0MT7UY5UR002LD5U), "Add a Magnet power up" (AH-0MT7VE4SX0005A8V), "Add an extra life power up" (AH-0MT7UX8LE0072MR3) — semantics source for P7/P9/P8 (P3/P4/P6 remain as defined in GDD §4.4).
- GDD items (completed): "Game Design Document for AI_Hell" (AH-0MT7O8KCY0059RA5).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Dependency:** this item assumes the non-combat gym (AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT) lands first (PowerUp lifecycle, catalogue, HUD, constants). If that item is delayed, the combat scene work is blocked — do not build parallel copies of the lifecycle/HUD.
- **Assumption — ship-aimed fire:** Scout's `tryFireAimedBullet` currently aims at a fixed demo target; the combat scene requires bullets aimed at the ship's live position. Implement by parameterising the aim target (small, contained change) rather than duplicating the Scout entity.
- **Assumption — teleport safe spot:** "nearest safe spot in the travel direction" = first empty position along the travel ray where no enemy body or bullet occupies a safety-radius disc (tunable, proposal 3× ship size), clamped to screen bounds; fallback = nearest on-screen safe position (GDD); P6 granted on arrival.
- **Assumption — hit response flash/reset:** a hit without shield/phase shift flashes the ship and repositions it (or grants brief invulnerability) — exact demo values tunable; no lives, no game over (operator Q8).
- **Assumption — scout formation counts as the "low-level threat":** default V-formation of ~6 scouts with drift (as GymScout), SHOOT toggle default OFF so the operator/player can turn fire on for the demo.
- **Scope-creep guard:** E2/E3/E4/E5/Boss threats, weapon autofire, lives/score, leaderboard, and the non-combat power-ups (P5/P8/P9) are out of scope; record any extras as linked work items.
- **Risk — sibling drift:** same constants/mechanics as the two sibling gyms; coordinate to keep the shared lifecycle consistent (extract a shared util if a third consumer appears).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (this round): "Which enemies constitute 'low level enemy threats' — reuse existing E1 Scout/E2 Diver/E3 Tank entities with bullet-firing, or generic placeholders?" — Answer (operator): **"1. Just use scout (with shooting)"** — the combat scene reuses the existing E1 Scout entity with its shooting enabled. Source: interactive reply.
- Q2 (this round): "Ship hit response in the combat gym — (a) lives with respawn (3 lives), (b) simple flash/reset without a lives counter, (c) other?" — Answer (operator): **"2. b"** — simple flash/reset, no lives counter (pure demo). Source: interactive reply.
- Q3 (scope split, previous round): "Separate the combat-coupled power-ups (P3/P4/P6/P7) into their own work item and combat scene with low-level enemy threats?" — Answer (operator): **"Separate out the combat coupled items into a different work item and different combat scene. That scene should contain low level enemy threats."** — implemented as this item; the threat-free gym (AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT) keeps P5/P8/P9 and the shared lifecycle/HUD. Source: interactive reply.

- **AH-0MT994ESD000RP1Q** – Create E1 Scout gym scene (completed)
- **AH-0MTAJO038004ILN8** – Gym index browser crash from bundled test files (completed)

# Diver has no audio (AH-0MTCO1LGD0082SVG)

**Headline:** The E2 Diver enemy is silent on its player-facing events: its spread bursts (3–5 projectiles, fired during a dive) produce no fire sound, and — per producer decision — its destruction should use a distinct Diver-specific sound rather than the shared generic burst. Add a Diver-specific fire sound played once per spread burst (procedural Web Audio, safe no-op without an AudioContext) and a distinct Diver destruction sound, wired through a minimal optional seam in the base `GymFormationScene` so it plays exactly once per destruction (no double-play). No firing advance cue is added (producer decision).

## Problem statement

The E2 Diver entity (`src/entities/Diver.ts`) plays no audio on its firing event: `tryFireSpreadBurst()` spawns 3–5 projectiles silently. Its destruction currently relies on the shared `playDestructionSound()` given to all enemies by `GymFormationScene`, but the producer wants a distinct Diver-specific destruction sound. The Diver breaks the GDD §7.3 audio-feedback design (enemy fire should be audible) and is inconsistent with its peers (Scout plays a fire sound, Tank plays a cue+thump, Swarm has a burst sound).

## Users

- **Players** — need audible feedback when a diver fires its spread burst (danger cue) and a distinct destruction sound so a diver explosion is distinguishable from Scout/Tank/Swarm explosions.
- **AI agents / developers implementing AI_Hell** — need Diver audio to follow the established procedural-audio pattern (`src/audio/effects.ts`) and the enemy core-library best practices so the shared base scene is not broken and headless tests stay green.

### Example user stories

- As a player, I want to hear a distinct sound when a diver fires its spread burst so I can react to the projectiles.
- As a player, I want a diver's destruction to sound different from other enemies so I can tell what kind of enemy I just destroyed.
- As a developer, I want Diver audio implemented via the existing `effects.ts` helpers and a minimal, backward-compatible seam in the base scene so it degrades to a safe no-op in headless tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Diver fire sound** — A new `playDiverFireSound()` exists in `src/audio/effects.ts` (distinct from the Scout blip, the Swarm buzz, and the Tank thump — e.g. a short low/nasal crack appropriate to the dive), played exactly **once per spread burst** (not once per projectile; the 3–5 bullet burst shares one sound).
- **No advance cue** — No firing advance cue (≥ 500 ms tell) is added to the Diver path; the fire sound plays at the moment the burst is fired. A test or explicit no-op documents that no cue helper is wired in.
- **Distinct destruction sound** — A new `playDiverDestructionSound()` exists in `src/audio/effects.ts` (distinct from the shared destruction burst and the Diver fire sound), played exactly **once per diver destruction** with no double-play of the shared `playDestructionSound()`. The Diver entity must NOT call a destruction sound in `playExplosion()`.
- **Wiring seam** — The base `GymFormationScene` gains a minimal optional per-entity hook (e.g. optional `playDestructionAudio?()` on `FormationSceneEntity`, mirroring the existing `setAimTarget?()` precedent) used by the two enemy-destruction call sites (`explodeRandom()` and `_handleCollisions()`); entities without the hook (Scout/Tank/Swarm/Phaser) keep the shared `playDestructionSound()`. Existing base-scene and enemy tests must pass unchanged.
- **Safe degradation** — All new audio calls are safe no-ops without a working `AudioContext` (headless tests, browsers without Web Audio), preserving the `effects.ts` contract.
- **Documentation** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README (if it lists per-enemy audio), and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (the §3.2 scene-table row for `GymDiver` currently lists audio as "none"; §6/§7 should note the optional per-entity destruction-sound seam).
- **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes (no CI/CD pipeline tests).

## Constraints

- Procedural Web Audio only — no audio assets (existing `effects.ts` pattern).
- Follow enemy core-library best practices (`docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`); the base `GymFormationScene` already plays destruction sounds for all enemy gyms — the implementer must avoid double-play when the Diver switches to a distinct sound.
- The base-scene seam must be backward compatible: entities that do not opt in keep current behaviour (shared sound).
- Audio functions must degrade to safe no-ops in headless environments.
- Do not include CI/CD pipeline tests.

## Existing state

- `src/entities/Diver.ts` — `tryFireSpreadBurst()` fires 3–5 projectiles silently (`DIVER_BURST_COUNT = 4`, `DIVER_FIRE_INTERVAL = 1000` ms, bursts fire during the dive); no audio imports, no sound calls. `playExplosion()` plays only VFX.
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — has `playSpawnSound`, `playDestructionSound`, `playTankDestructionSound` (intentionally unwired dead code), Tank cue/thump, power-up/weapon cues, `playSwarmBurstSound`, and — after AH-0MTCO1LDA008RA19 — `playScoutFireSound`/`playScoutAdvanceCue`; **no Diver-specific fire or destruction sound exists**.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — base class plays `playSpawnSound()` at spawn and `playDestructionSound()` in `explodeRandom()` (line ~305) and in `_handleCollisions()` (line ~585, enemy destroyed by player bullet). `FormationSceneEntity` already has an optional `setAimTarget?()` seam — the precedent for an optional per-entity hook.
- Reference patterns: **Tank** (`GymTank.update()`) plays cue+thump once per radial burst at scene level by comparing bullet counts; **Scout** plays an entity-level fire sound once per aimed shot; **Swarm** plays a scene-level burst sound per volley.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §3.2 — scene table lists `GymDiver` audio as "none"; §7 documents destruction-sound ownership (base class) and the no-double-play rule.
- `README.md` line ~372 documents the Scout audio in the `src/audio/effects.ts` bullet — the Diver entry should be added there if the bullet is per-enemy (verified: it is a single bullet listing effects; update to mention Diver fire/destruction sounds).
- `src/entities/Diver.test.ts` — existing tests cover rendering, aim-target retargeting, and dive-start snapshots; no audio tests. `src/scenes/gym/GymDiver.test.ts` covers scene behaviour; no audio tests.

## Desired change

- **Diver entity**: call `playDiverFireSound()` exactly once per spread burst inside `tryFireSpreadBurst()` (when a burst is actually produced). Add an implementation of the optional destruction-audio hook (e.g. `playDestructionAudio()` → `playDiverDestructionSound()`), and leave `playExplosion()` free of any sound call (base scene owns play timing).
- **Base scene seam**: add the optional hook to `FormationSceneEntity` and prefer it (fall back to `playDestructionSound()`) at the two enemy-destruction call sites.
- **New sounds**: add `playDiverFireSound()` (short, distinct burst-blip) and `playDiverDestructionSound()` (distinct, e.g. a deeper/lower variant of the destruction burst) to `src/audio/effects.ts`, both safe no-ops without an `AudioContext`.

**Key Files:**

- `src/entities/Diver.ts` — add once-per-burst `playDiverFireSound()` call in `tryFireSpreadBurst()`; implement the optional destruction-audio hook; keep `playExplosion()` silent re: sound.
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — add `playDiverFireSound()` and `playDiverDestructionSound()` (procedural Web Audio, safe no-op guard).
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — add optional `playDestructionAudio?()` to `FormationSceneEntity`; use it (falling back to the shared sound) in `explodeRandom()` and `_handleCollisions()`.
- `src/entities/Diver.test.ts` — add fire-sound-once-per-burst test and destruction-sound-once/no-double-play test (spy/mock the `effects` module).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymDiver.test.ts` — scene-level regression: audio no-op degradation; destruction hook used exactly once with no double-play.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts` — regression: entities without the hook still play the shared sound once (if needed).
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — update the §3.2 table row for `GymDiver` (audio column) and §6/§7 (optional per-entity destruction-sound seam + no-double-play note).
- `README.md` — update the `src/audio/effects.ts` bullet (line ~372) to mention the Diver fire/destruction sounds.

## Related work

- **Scout has no audio (AH-0MTCO1LDA008RA19)** — completed; the sibling item that added Scout fire sound + advance cue following the same `effects.ts` pattern (reference for this item).
- **Swarm has no audio (AH-0MTCO1L74003CAQJ)** — completed; the sibling item that added the Swarm burst sound.
- **Create E2 Diver gym scene (AH-0MT99G6310070UXM)** — completed; the scene and entity that need the audio.
- **Write ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md best-practice guide (AH-0MTAN4X5D009D7U6)** — completed; §6/§7 documents audio ownership and the no-double-play rule that the distinct destruction sound must respect.
- **Fix Diver.ts: lock x during dive and smooth return (AH-0MTEI361E000IXYB)** — completed; recent Diver behaviour changes (context for the entity).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Base-scene seam (medium)**: adding an optional hook to the shared `GymFormationScene` touches all five gyms. Mitigation: it is a backward-compatible optional method (precedent: `setAimTarget?()`); entities that omit it keep the shared sound; existing base-scene tests must pass unchanged.
- **Double-play risk (high)**: the Diver entity must NOT call a destruction sound in `playExplosion()`; the base scene owns play timing via the hook (design doc §7). The once-only guarantee is an AC with tests.
- **Fire-sound granularity**: `tryFireSpreadBurst()` returns the whole 3–5 bullet burst, so calling the sound once inside it when a burst is produced satisfies "once per volley" (analogous to Tank's scene-level once-per-burst, but entity-level since each diver dives independently). Assumption: per-entity call site is acceptable; if the producer preferred scene-level, that is a small adjustment.
- **Testability**: existing enemy tests do not exercise audio; new tests will spy/mock `src/audio/effects` to assert call counts/ordering in headless runs.
- **Scope creep**: no advance cue (producer decision Q2). No other audio work for Scout/Tank/Swarm/Phaser is implied (pre-existing gaps are out of scope; record separately if discovered).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1**: Should the Diver have a fire sound for its spread bursts, and at what granularity? — **Answer (producer): "1. a + b"** — (a) a single sound per spread burst (once per volley, not per projectile) AND (b) a distinct Diver-specific fire sound (not reusing an existing sound). Source: interactive reply 2026-08-30 (session herdr-1788063396-1018602-1665).
- **Q2**: Should the Diver play a firing advance audio cue (≥ 500 ms lead, like Scout/Phaser)? — **Answer (producer): "no"** — no advance cue; the fire sound alone is sufficient. Source: interactive reply 2026-08-30.
- **Q3**: Should the Diver reuse the shared `playDestructionSound()` or have a distinct destruction sound? — **Answer (producer): "distinct"** — a distinct Diver-specific destruction sound (wired so it plays once per destruction; no double-play with the base scene). # Player cannot be moved in enemy and power-up gym scenes — Intake Brief

## Problem Statement

Since switchable player control types landed (AH-0MTF0EFNZ000RPVD), the player cannot be moved in the enemy gym scenes or the power-up gym scene when the saved control scheme is **asteroids**. The player loads the saved ship config (which now persists `controlScheme`), installs `AsteroidsModel` (which expects `{ forward, turnLeft, turnRight }` input), but the gym scenes still feed input through the legacy `keysToInput()` which always emits the 4-directional `{ up, down, left, right }` shape — the Asteroids model ignores it, so there is no thrust and no rotation.

## Users

- **Player / developer playtesting** — wants the same playable controls in every gym scene, honouring whatever scheme was saved in the ship-config gym.
- **AI agents / automated tests** — need scheme-aware input wiring that is unit-testable without booting a Phaser scene.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Saved scheme honoured in all affected scenes:** With the **asteroids** scheme saved, the player moves in every enemy gym scene (E1 Scout, E2 Diver, E3 Tank, E4 Phaser, E5 Swarm, Boss) and the power-up gym scene: W/Up = forward thrust, A/Left + S/Right = turn (matching `GymPlayer`).
- **AC2 — 4-directional backward compatible:** With the 4-directional scheme saved, movement in those scenes is unchanged (WASD/arrows) — no regression.
- **AC3 — Scheme-aware input wiring:** `GymFormationScene._readPlayerInput()` and `GymPowerUps._readInput()` (and any remaining legacy `keysToInput` user) route input through the pluggable `InputHandler` classes keyed off `player.getScheme()` — the same pattern `GymPlayer` already uses (`AsteroidsInputHandler` / `FourDirectionalInputHandler`) — rather than the hard-wired 4-directional mapping.
- **AC4 — Validation/tests:** Automated tests cover both schemes' input mapping for the affected scenes (per-scene assertions + a regression test for the asteroids scheme), and the full project test suite passes with the new changes.
- **AC5 — Documentation:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries (incl. the player-in-enemy-gym convention doc AH-0MTECNKXX001XBLJ).

## Constraints

- **Interim fix in the current scene structure** — explicitly NOT blocked on the Enemy Design tooling item (AH-0MTFP7EIC004F1MN); that refactor will supersede this per-scene wiring (dependency note recorded).
- Backward compatible: the 4-directional scheme must keep working untouched.
- Scope is bug-fix only: no new control schemes, no enemy config work, no refactor of the scenes themselves.
- Note: **GymWeapons** (weapons gym scene) uses the identical legacy `keysToInput` pattern and is affected the same way — in scope (same one-line fix pattern).

## Existing State

- `Player` constructor and `setConfig` load the saved ship config (`loadShipConfig()`), which persists `controlScheme` + `asteroidsRotationSpeed` (src/core/config.ts); the ship installs the matching pluggable model (`AsteroidsModel` / `FourDirectionalModel`) and expects the matching input shape (src/entities/Player.ts:194-215, 342-343, 411-432).
- `GymPlayer` (ship-config gym) already uses the pluggable handlers: `AsteroidsInputHandler.mapInput(raw)` / `FourDirectionalInputHandler.mapInput(raw)` keyed off `player.getScheme()` (src/scenes/gym/GymPlayer.ts:88, 338-353) — this scene works.
- Enemy gyms extend `GymFormationScene`, whose `_readPlayerInput()` calls `keysToInput(cursors, wasd)` (src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts:495-499) — always 4-directional.
- `GymPowerUps` (extends `Phaser.Scene`) calls `keysToInput(cursors, wasd)` at src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUps.ts:241.
- `GymWeapons` (extends `Phaser.Scene`) calls `keysToInput(cursors, wasd)` at src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts:353.
- Pluggable classes already exist in src/utils/movementModel.ts: `FourDirectionalInputHandler` / `AsteroidsInputHandler` (map raw `{ cursors, wasd }` key state to the scheme-appropriate `ControlInput` shape).

## Desired Change

- Replace the legacy `keysToInput` wiring in `GymFormationScene` (base, fixing all six enemy gyms at once) and in `GymPowerUps` (and `GymWeapons`) with scheme-aware `InputHandler` routing mirroring `GymPlayer._readInput()`.
- Add/extend unit tests asserting scheme-correct input mapping per scene, plus a regression test that an asteroids-scheme player in these scenes receives `{ forward, turnLeft, turnRight }`.
- Record a dependency/related note on AH-0MTFP7EIC004F1MN (Enemy Design tooling) so the config-driven restructure supersedes this per-scene wiring.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — `_readPlayerInput()` fixed to use scheme-aware `InputHandler` (fixes E1–E5 + Boss)
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUps.ts` — `_readInput()` fixed the same way
- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts` — `_readInput()` fixed the same way (discovered affected site)
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPlayer.ts` — reference implementation for the scheme-aware pattern (no change expected)
- `src/utils/movementModel.ts` — `AsteroidsInputHandler` / `FourDirectionalInputHandler` (already exist, consumed)
- `src/utils/input.ts` — legacy `keysToInput` helper (may be retired if no remaining users)
- Tests: `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUps.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.test.ts`, plus per-scene gym tests

## Related Work

- **AH-0MTF0EFNZ000RPVD** — Alternative player control (completed; introduced the switchable schemes + persistence that caused this regression)
- **AH-0MTD0Z0Y7003T1NT** — Add player to each Enemy Gym scene (in-progress; wired player presence into these scenes)
- **AH-0MTFP7EIC004F1MN** — Enemy Design tooling (open, stage idea; the config-driven restructure this interim fix must not block on; dependency/related note recorded per operator decision)
- **AH-0MTECNKXX001XBLJ** — Docs: player-in-enemy-gym convention (completed; may need updating for scheme-aware input)
